MATTHEW.|35}}</noinclude>he that hath, to him shal be giuen, and he shal abound: but he that hath not, from him shal be taken avvay that also vvhich he hath. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=13}}† Therfore in parables I speake to them: because seeing they see not, and {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ When Gods word is preached, they proprely haue eares to heare, that haue hartes to obey: and they hearing do not heare, which heare by sense of their body, and obey not by consent of their hartes. ''Aug. de dono perseu. c. 14''.}}∷ hearing they heare not, neither do they vnderstand: {{verse|chapter=13|verse=14}}† and the prophecie of Esay is fulfilled in them, vvhich saith, ''With hearing shal you heare, and you shal not vnderstand: and seeing shal you see, and you shal not see''. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=15}}† ''For the hart of this people is vvaxed grosse, and vvith their eares they haue heauily heard, and their eies {{sup|‖}} they haue shut: lest at any time they may see with their eies, and heare with their eares, and vnderstand vvith their hart and be conuerted, and I may heale them''. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=16}}† But blessed are your eyes because they doe see, and your eares because they doe heare. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=17}}† For amen I say to you, that {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 10, 23.''}}* many Prophets and iust men haue desired to see the things that you see, and haue not seen them: and to heare the things that you heare, and haue not heard them. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=18}}† Heare you therfore the parable of the sovver.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=19}}† Euery one that heareth the vvord of the kingdom and vnderstandeth not, there cometh the vvicked one, and catcheth avvay that vvhich vvas sovven in his hart: this is he that vvas sovven by the vvay side. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=20}}† And he that vvas sovven vpon rockie places: this is he that heareth the vvord, and incontinent receiueth it vvith ioy, {{verse|chapter=13|verse=21}}† yet hath he not roote in him self, but is for a time: and vvhen there falleth tribulation and persecution for the vvord, he is by and by scandalized. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=22}}† And he that vvas sovven among thornes, this is he that heareth the vvord, and the carefulnes of this vvorld and the deceitfulnes of riches choketh vp the vvord, and he becometh fruitles. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=23}}† But he that vvas sovven vpon good ground: this is he that heareth the vvord, and vnderstandeth, and bringeth fruite, and yeldeth some an hundred-fold, and other threescore, and an other thirtie.

{{verse|chapter=13|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel vpō the 5 Sunday after the Epiphanie.}}An other parable he proposed to them, saying, The kingdom of heauen is resembled to a man that sovved good seede in his field. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=25}}† But vvhen men vvere a sleepe, his enemy came and {{sup|‖}} ouersovved cockle among the vvheate, and vvent his vvay. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=26}}† And vvhen the blade vvas shot vp, and had brought forth fruite, then appeared also the cockle. {{verse|chapter=13|verse=27}}† And the seruants of the goodman of the house comming said to him, Sir, didst thou not sovv good seede in thy field? Whence then hath it cockle? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=28}}† And he said to them, The enemy man hath done this. And the seruants said to him, Wilt thou vve goe and gather it vp? {{verse|chapter=13|verse=29}}† And he said, No: {{sup|‖}} lest perhaps<noinclude>{{rh||E ij|gathering}}</noinclude>
